title: Series distinction combines colour, pattern and direct label so a colour-blind reader reads the same distinction
asA: reader with a colour-vision deficiency using the shipped surface
iWant: each series on a multi-series chart to carry colour, a distinguishing pattern and a direct label at the series
soThat: the series distinction is legible without relying on colour perception alone (WCAG 1.4.1)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered chart with N series, the series distinction combines colour, pattern (dashed line, hatched fill or a marker shape) and a direct label at the series; every series in the DOM carries a data-pattern attribute or a stroke-dasharray or an SVG pattern fill reference and a labelled text node adjacent to the series. Probed by the application-charts pack check AC-18102-1 (Playwright drives the browser to the chart route, reads the accessibility tree and the DOM, and asserts every series carries at least one non-colour attribute plus a direct label). The runner has no vision-deficiency emulation seam today, so the check is proven at the DOM level (colour is only one of the three cues); the README names the vision-deficiency simulation gap under known mechanism-reach gaps.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every series carries colour plus a non-colour pattern attribute plus a direct label

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered single-series chart, the AC-18102-1 rule does not apply (single-series distinction is not a WCAG 1.4.1 concern); the pack records applicable false for the check on the surface and no browser assertion runs. The blueprint's README names the single-series exemption under known mechanism-reach gaps.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the AC-18102-1 rule does not apply and the pack records applicable false

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered multi-series chart whose series distinction relies on the shipped accessible palette AND a distinguishing pattern, when the deuteranopia simulation is applied to a screenshot of the surface, the series remain visually distinct (a pattern still parses through the simulation); a chart whose only distinction is a colour indistinguishable under the simulation fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered multi-series chart under a deuteranopia simulation
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the simulated screenshot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the series remain visually distinct through the pattern and label; a colour-only distinction fails

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered multi-series chart whose legend is present but no series carries a direct label at the series, the pack fails the check per REQ-002 (a legend entry alone does not satisfy the AC); a passing chart carries a direct label at each series either inside the plot area or immediately adjacent to the series line, bar or slice.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered multi-series chart with a legend but no direct series labels
acceptanceCriteria.then: the check fails; a passing chart carries a direct series label at each series (not only in the legend)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered multi-series chart with more series than the shipped palette provides colours for (a 20-series chart against an 8-colour palette), the shell cycles the palette AND changes the pattern so the pattern-plus-index combination stays unique across series; two series that share both colour AND pattern fail the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered chart with more series than the palette carries colours
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects series colour and pattern combinations
acceptanceCriteria.then: each series has a unique (colour, pattern) combination; two series sharing both fail the check
